purpose: Persistent published-event ledger; retains deleted-duplicate tombstones

stories.title: Spotlight fees are heading back to court. What does it mean for actors?
stories.description: Equity’s appeal is set for 24 November. Here is what is at stake for working actors.

stories.title: Bradford venue faces closure
stories.description: Theatre in the Mill is due to close on 31 March 2027.

stories.title: The UK screen sector in numbers
stories.description: A briefing on the BFI’s latest quarterly figures.

stories.title: A wrong turn on the way home from IKEA leads to Dante’s dark wood
stories.description: Tania Khan’s I Can See the Sun brings surreal new writing to the Hope Theatre in Islington, with remaining performances through 21 November.

stories.title: Dogstar: a stranded crew, a restless new playwright and divided critics
stories.description: Daisy Hall’s Arctic-set dark comedy at Hampstead Downstairs has drawn contrasting responses, with praise for its three performers.

stories.title: The Moth: can two men ever escape the history that binds them?
stories.description: Paul Herzberg’s London premiere at the Finborough has inspired contrasting critical reactions to its exploration of apartheid and forgiveness.

stories.title: Barbara Broccoli takes the helm at the NFTS
stories.description: The Bond producer becomes the National Film and Television School’s first woman president, as the school prepares to open a new building in January.

stories.title: Bectu renews its call for safer creative workplaces
stories.description: The union is urging employers to implement the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority’s framework, with particular attention to reporting concerns.

stories.title: The Old Vic opens a new chapter with Rupert Goold’s first season
stories.description: Four productions lead the incoming artistic director’s 2027 programme, with public booking due to open on 16 November.

stories.title: Horrible Things: Frankie Thompson makes discomfort a comic instrument
stories.description: Two critics consider the clown’s unsettling, inventive solo show, now at Soho Theatre until 21 November.

stories.title: Relative Motion: when a romance starts obeying different laws
stories.description: Stephanie Greenwood’s new play uses physics to examine a relationship that moves from attraction towards coercion.

stories.title: Lover Girl: Temi Wilkey takes the solo show into stranger territory
stories.description: Critical responses differ over the structure of Wilkey’s solo performance, blending stand-up, R&B and theatrical surrealism at Soho Upstairs.

stories.title: Lear: Ian McKellen returns to a role that refuses to let him go
stories.description: A new play at the Yard Theatre brings Shakespeare into conversation with the actor’s own working life, opening on 17 November.

stories.title: The National Theatre takes its name seriously
stories.description: A four-year programme backed by up to £15 million aims to bring theatre and creative training to more than 100,000 young people across England.

stories.title: Edinburgh Fringe raises the price of taking a chance
stories.description: The Fringe Society has announced higher show registration fees for 2027, ending a freeze that began in 2007.

stories.title: The Yard makes room for Sondheim
stories.description: Jay Miller will direct the Hackney Wick theatre’s first musical, Company, ahead of a transfer to Theatr Clwyd and a national tour.

stories.title: Attention: the art of listening when the script can change
stories.description: Jules Head and Georgia Bruce bring their formally adventurous two-hander to the Bush Studio, with its original Dublin cast.

stories.title: Doublespeak: the classics have a few things to say about spin
stories.description: A new early modern theatre festival in Camberwell gives emerging performers a chance to examine the politics of language.

stories.title: The Café: a little shelter in a city that rarely sits still
stories.description: Roccia Zhang’s multilingual play brings four London lives together at the Etcetera Theatre during Voila! Theatre Festival.

stories.title: Cranford: the quiet art of making a room laugh
stories.description: Tamsin Greig leads an ensemble in Richmond, where Elizabeth Gaskell’s village becomes a study in comic timing and private grief.

stories.title: Wits End: a funeral with rather too much unfinished business
stories.description: Estée Stimler’s family comedy puts grief and obligation in a room of fifty-five seats.

stories.title: Roleplay: when the personal brand becomes the part
stories.description: Hannah Reilly’s solo show reaches its final week at Soho Theatre, with critics admiring the performer more consistently than the play.

stories.title: Rambert takes It’s a Sin back to the dancefloor
stories.description: A new trailer offers a first look at the dance adaptation of Russell T Davies’s television drama, ahead of its Manchester premiere.

stories.title: Hamnet leaves Stratford for its first UK tour
stories.description: The RSC and Neal Street stage adaptation will begin a nationwide tour in Salford in September 2027, with casting still to come.

stories.title: Matt Henry takes the classroom in To Sir, With Love
stories.description: The Olivier Award-winning performer leads a new musical adaptation touring the UK from April 2027.

stories.title: Equity's AI deal gives performers a vote on their digital doubles
stories.description: A proposed three-year Equity–Pact agreement promises new safeguards for performers’ likenesses, self-tapes and pay. Members now decide whether to accept it.

stories.title: Sirocco: the Noël Coward play that refused to behave
stories.description: The Finborough revisits Coward’s notorious early failure, restoring censored material and asking whether a scandal can outlive its original audience.

stories.title: The Master Builder: ambition begins to look like fear
stories.description: Greg Hicks stars in David Edgar’s version of Ibsen at the Arcola, where the older artist’s dread of being replaced remains painfully current.

stories.title: The BFI backs a more thoughtful approach to screen technology
stories.description: New funding for NFTS and Falmouth aims to help independent filmmakers work with emerging technology without losing sight of the people involved.

stories.title: The self-tape is a performance, not a camera test

stories.title: Before signing away a performance, read the digital clauses
stories.description: Why consent, duration and future uses deserve careful attention when actors review agreements involving recorded performances.

stories.title: On a small stage, there is nowhere for an actor to hide

stories.title: New writing needs an audience, not a verdict
stories.description: Why the first public life of a new play is a conversation between writer, actors and a room full of strangers.

stories.title: The quiet virtuosity of stepping into someone else's part
stories.description: An appreciation of covers, understudies and the craft of keeping a small production alive when its cast changes.

stories.title: The casting brief is telling you more than the character's age
stories.description: What a casting notice reveals about a role, and what an actor should resist reading into it.

stories.title: What a showreel can prove in its first minute

stories.title: The rehearsal room rewards a better question

stories.title: When the lights go down, the smallest theatre grows larger

stories.title: The pause before the laugh belongs to the actor

stories.title: One chair, several worlds: the intelligence of a small set
stories.description: How a carefully chosen object can carry a play further than elaborate scenery in an intimate theatre.

stories.title: The recall is not a second first audition
stories.description: How actors can carry a strong initial choice into a recall while remaining available to direction.

stories.title: An acting CV should make the work easy to find
stories.description: A practical look at credits, training and why a clear acting CV beats an impressive-looking inventory.

stories.title: The microphone is not a substitute for listening
stories.description: Why voice performance depends on intention, distance and a believable relationship beyond the recording booth.

stories.title: The quiet authority of the fringe stage manager
stories.description: An appreciation of the organisation and judgement that keep intimate London productions coherent.

stories.title: The interval is a dramatic decision, not a courtesy
stories.description: What an uninterrupted performance can offer a small theatre, and what it asks of its audience.

stories.title: A prop can remember what a character cannot say
stories.description: How ordinary objects acquire dramatic weight in the close quarters of fringe theatre.

stories.title: The reader is part of the audition, even when unseen
stories.description: Why the off-camera voice, listening and the space between lines matter more than an elaborate self-tape set-up.

stories.title: An agent meeting is a conversation, not a coronation
stories.description: What actors can usefully ask about representation, communication and expectations before agreeing to work together.

stories.title: A synthetic voice still raises a human question
stories.description: An actor-focused explanation of why recording consent and future voice reuse should be discussed separately.

stories.title: In a fringe theatre, the audience is part of the weather
stories.description: How proximity changes an actor's scale, attention and relationship with a small London audience.

stories.title: The fringe rehearsal clock is always running
stories.description: A practical essay on protecting discovery and ensemble trust when a small production has limited rehearsal time.

stories.title: The sound of a small stage includes silence
stories.description: Why intimate theatre needs restraint in sound design as much as invention.

stories.title: Elsinore leads the 2026 British Independent Film Awards nominations
stories.description: Simon Stone’s Ian Charleson drama leads the BIFA field with 12 nominations ahead of December’s ceremony.

stories.title: The Sorcerer’s Apprentice prepares for its Manchester stage premiere
stories.description: A ten-strong cast brings Richard Hough and Alexander S Bermange’s musical to HOME from 27th November.

stories.title: Elsinore begins its US cinema release ahead of January’s UK opening
stories.description: Simon Stone’s film about Ian Charleson reached selected US cinemas on 20th November; its UK release is set for 29th January.

stories.title: The Human Voice at the Cockpit puts Elliot Pritchard on the line
stories.description: A new queer-inflected adaptation of Jean Cocteau’s monologue runs from 24th November to 5th December.

stories.title: Fly, You Fools! brings a miniature Middle-earth to Southwark Playhouse
stories.description: Recent Cutbacks’ Lord of the Rings parody opens at Southwark Playhouse Borough on 25th November.

stories.title: The History Boys launches an open search for eight West End pupils
stories.description: Nicholas Hytner’s return to Alan Bennett’s play is inviting unrepresented actors to audition in London and Leeds.

stories.title: The Watermill brings Pinocchio back with Jax Guerrero in the title role
stories.description: The Newbury theatre’s festive revival begins on 25th November, with returning performers and a new lead.

stories.title: Goblin arrives at Park Theatre with Derek Mitchell’s dark coming-of-age solo show
stories.description: Derek Mitchell’s one-person production plays at Park Theatre until 5th December.

stories.title: The Silence and the Noise returns to Park Theatre with a Papatango Prize pedigree
stories.description: Tom Powell’s two-hander, directed by George Turvey, runs from 25th November to 12th December.

stories.title: Ramin Gray revisits The Ugly One at Arcola Theatre
stories.description: Marius von Mayenburg’s satire of appearance and identity plays in Arcola’s Studio 2 until 19th December.

stories.title: Phantom’s fortieth year brings a new trio to His Majesty’s Theatre
stories.description: Kimberly Blake, Kate Graham and Luke Kempner join the West End production from 23rd November, with Ashley Gilmour returning as Raoul.

stories.title: Dick Whittington heads to Islington as King’s Head unveils its winter panto
stories.description: Andrew Pollard’s family pantomime opens on 24th November, with Joseph Vella, Victoria Scone and River Medway in the cast.

stories.title: WhatsOnStage Awards close nominations ahead of December shortlist
stories.description: Public nominations for the 27th awards closed at noon on 24th November; the shortlist is due on 10th December.

stories.title: Joel Montague turns green as Leeds Playhouse stages a new Grinch
stories.description: Tom Wright directs the Broadway musical’s new UK production in the Quarry, with performances continuing until 16th January.

stories.title: Edinburgh’s Traverse announces a spring season built around new writing
stories.description: Linda McLean’s The Ferry, a Murakami adaptation and Tafadzwa Muchenje’s Ripples feature in the programme announced on 23rd November.

stories.title: Pink Rabbit transfers to Soho Theatre after its Edinburgh debut
stories.description: Farah Ashraf’s solo play, directed by Alessandro Babalola, runs in Soho Upstairs from 24th November to 12th December.

stories.title: Majenin brings a Palestinian romantic comedy to Theatre503
stories.description: Marena Riyad’s Edinburgh Fringe two-hander runs at the Battersea venue from 23rd to 28th November.

stories.title: After Today revisits Bill Grundy at the Hope Theatre
stories.description: Tim Connery’s play opens on 24th November, with Alex Dee as Grundy and Kevin McNally directing.

stories.title: Samantha Morton to receive the BFI Fellowship
stories.description: The BFI announced its highest honour for Morton on 23rd November, with a January presentation and a June retrospective.

stories.title: Bailey West makes his stage debut in the touring cast of Punch
stories.description: Nottingham Playhouse announced the cast on 19th November for James Graham’s play, touring from January to April 2027.

stories.title: Stoppard’s Jumpers begins its Hampstead revival with Rhea Norwood and James Corrigan
stories.description: Blanche McIntyre directs the comedy’s first London staging in more than two decades, with previews starting on 25th November.

stories.title: Shakespeare’s Cousin enters its final week at the White Bear
stories.description: Jonathan Moore’s new play about Robert Southwell runs in Kennington until 28th November.

stories.title: It’s a Wonderful Life goes on air at Jermyn Street Theatre
stories.description: Jessica Lazar’s radio-on-stage production runs from 19th November to 3rd January, with six multi-roling performers.

stories.title: Intermission Youth puts Julius Caesar in a modern classroom at Omnibus
stories.description: Darren Raymond’s play, directed by Stephanie Badaru, continues at the Clapham theatre until 5th December.

stories.title: Sheffield’s Crucible opens Singin’ in the Rain with Grant Almirall
stories.description: Jonathan Church directs the musical’s Christmas engagement, beginning on 26th November and running to 16th January.

stories.title: Starlight Express rolls into cinemas from Wembley
stories.description: Brett Sullivan’s film of the London stage revival receives its international cinema release on 26th November.

stories.title: Sanjeev Bhaskar joins the BFI as archive ambassador
stories.description: The actor’s appointment on 19th November accompanies a preservation project for more than 10,000 hours of breakfast television.

stories.title: Mark McAuley brings Gogol’s Diary of a Mad Man to the Old Red Lion
stories.description: The Edinburgh Fringe transfer plays six performances in Islington from 24th to 28th November.

stories.title: Mary Bennet takes the lead in Park Theatre’s Christmas at Pemberley
stories.description: Sarah Meadows directs the UK premiere of Lauren Gunderson and Margot Melcon’s Austen sequel from 2nd December.

stories.title: Hathaleen concludes its Greenwich Theatre studio run
stories.description: Louis Linsey’s play, developed from his experiences in the West Bank, reaches its final scheduled performance on 26th November.

stories.title: Equity and ITC agree three years of minimum pay increases
stories.description: Independent theatre’s new agreement sets minimum weekly rates from April 2027, alongside plans for ethical casting and AI policies.

stories.title: Julianne Pundan to make her West End debut in Miss Saigon
stories.description: The principal cast announced on 26th November reunites touring performers for the musical’s return to the Prince Edward Theatre.

stories.title: In Pieces assembles its cast for a London stage production
stories.description: Joey Contreras’s musical follows six interlocking stories of love at The Other Palace from 6th February 2027.

stories.title: NERO puts an emperor’s appetite for performance centre stage
stories.description: Andrew Barth Feldman leads Steven Sater and Duncan Sheik’s musical at Southwark Playhouse Elephant until 5th December.

stories.title: Emily Woof’s REVOLVER moves between Beatlemania and the present
stories.description: Hamish McColl directs Woof’s Edinburgh transfer at Soho Theatre until 5th December.

stories.title: Private Jones brings signed language and sound together on stage
stories.description: Rose Ayling-Ellis and James Spence feature in Marshall Pailet’s musical opening at Southwark Playhouse Elephant on 14th December.
